content.value_statement: Frontend teams lose time when app patterns vary across routing, fetching, loading, and styling. This skill provides concise guidelines for Next.js, React, TypeScript, shadcn/ui, MUI, and TanStack Query.
actual_capabilities: Explains Server Component, Client Component, and Server Action patterns for Next.js App Router.
Provides React component patterns for React.FC props, lazy loading, and Suspense boundaries.
Documents data-fetching patterns with TanStack Query, Suspense, cache-first reads, and mutation invalidation.
Shows file organization guidance for feature directories, reusable components, APIs, hooks, helpers, and types.
Covers MUI styling, shadcn/ui usage, TypeScript standards, and performance optimization.
Includes complete example flows for user profiles, posts, routing, loading, and error handling.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not install dependencies or modify project files by itself.
Examples assume React, TypeScript, and modern frontend frameworks; other stacks need adaptation.
Some resources mention MUI and TanStack Router in addition to the Next.js and shadcn/ui summary.
It does not replace project-specific security, accessibility, or performance testing.

use_cases.title: Standardize a New Feature
use_cases.description: Plan routing, component boundaries, API services, hooks, loading states, and styles before building a feature.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Architecture
use_cases.description: Check whether a pull request follows shared patterns for Suspense, data fetching, TypeScript, and file layout.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a React Codebase
use_cases.description: Learn the expected conventions for components, styling, routing, cache behavior, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to plan a new page for [route]. Include component type, data fetching, loading state, error state, and styling choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to design a reusable [component]. Define props, state boundaries, UI library usage, accessibility needs, and file placement.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to refactor [screen] to TanStack Query with Suspense. Include cache keys, invalidation, loading behavior, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Feature Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines to review [feature folder]. Identify deviations in routing, components, API services, hooks, TypeScript, styling, and performance patterns.

output_examples.input: Plan a posts dashboard page with filters, a table, and edit actions.
output: Use a feature folder with API, hooks, components, types, and helpers.
Render the table inside a Suspense boundary and lazy load the heavy grid.
Use TanStack Query keys for the list, detail records, and mutations.
Add loading and error boundaries that preserve page layout.

output_examples.input: Review a profile editor for loading and error behavior.
output: Avoid early loading returns that replace the page structure.
Wrap independent sections in SuspenseLoader when data can load separately.
Use mutation success and error handlers for cache invalidation and user feedback.

output_examples.input: Organize a new feature that needs list, detail, and edit views.
output: Create a feature directory with API services, route components, reusable subcomponents, hooks, and shared types.
Keep generic UI components outside the feature only when they are reused across several areas.
Document public exports through the feature index file.

best_practices: Use Server Components or Suspense-based data flows unless interactivity requires client state.
Keep feature code organized by API services, hooks, components, helpers, and shared types.
Add loading, error, TypeScript, styling, and performance checks before marking frontend work complete.
anti_patterns: Do not add client-only components when server rendering or Suspense can handle the workflow.
Do not scatter API calls across components when a feature service layer exists.
Do not use early loading returns that cause layout shift or hide page structure.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits React and TypeScript frontend projects that use modern routing, component, data-fetching, and UI patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate working application code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples that an AI assistant can apply when writing or reviewing project code.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Next.js?
faq.answer: No. Next.js patterns are central, but several resources also cover TanStack Router and general React architecture.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Only limited frontend safety guidance is included. Use separate security review for authentication, authorization, and data exposure.

faq.question: How should teams use it during code review?
faq.answer: Ask the assistant to compare changed files against the documented patterns for data fetching, loading, file layout, TypeScript, and styling.
